fuse-mount-build-and-cleanup-stalls.scope: the repo and its A/B build trees live on two different mounts: /media/win_data is fuseblk (ntfs-3g) and /home is ext4. On FUSE the same `vite build` that takes 40-50s on ext4 sat in `transforming` for 15+ minutes at 2-6% CPU with wchan=request_wait_answer, `du` on a e2e artifact dir timed out, deleting node_modules took 13 minutes, vite dev reported ready after 63s and its first request took 30s+. This is what made the S3 browser rounds unusable in the 2026-09-16 session, and it is also why the benchmark numbers drift so much on this host.
fuse-mount-build-and-cleanup-stalls.unlock: run e2e and builds from an ext4 checkout (or move the repo), and keep e2e artifacts off the FUSE mount; the debt ledger row carries the measurements

e2e-readiness-predicate-flake.scope: e2e/utils/waits.ts expectDevServerReady polls /@vite/client from inside the test and intermittently times out at 120s on this host while the same URL answers in ~25ms from a shell; three occurrences in one session, each passing on rerun. Adjacent, the 180s per-test budget is sometimes too small for the heaviest cases on this host. The mechanism is recorded with its correction in docs/technical-debt.md §8 (`冷态 dev server 的首轮编译会顶穿就绪探测预算`): the cold first round compiles on the server's single event loop, so even static paths queue, and the case that pays for it is the FIRST of the round — re-measured during S7, where warming `/` alone took 293s while every later route took 7-10s, and a run that warmed only `/` still stalled on its second navigation.
e2e-readiness-predicate-flake.unlock: keep the readiness signal honest and stop paying the cold round per suite: either give the first case of a round its own budget (the ledger's second option), or land the ledger's first option — warm the target routes (including a session-detail route, which is where the mode content panels compile) to first paint before the round. S7 warmed with a scratch script outside the harness; the fix belongs in the harness's global setup. The ledger explicitly rules out enlarging APP_READY_TIMEOUT globally, because that also slows catching a server that is genuinely down.

mode-detail-personas-closure-observation.scope: the three `closed:false` observation bundles in e2e/regression/mode-detail-personas.spec.ts are about Work/Assistant identity and scope (Work presetCategoryId=null and its artifact empty state, Assistant not showing personal/project scope, the identity header missing scope/preset/inherited model source). plan §10 had assigned their conversion to real assertions to S7, but their subject matter belongs with the slices that own it.
mode-detail-personas-closure-observation.unlock: S9A/S9B convert them into expect() assertions when the Work and Assistant closures land; the session-product-header-projection entry (S9B) is the Header half of the third bundle

path-identity.scope: plan §11.2 requires a provable path identity, and S8 reconnaissance found there is none anywhere: zero inode/device/sameFile hits across core, schema and aigcfroge; `Project.resolve` (packages/core/src/project.ts:110-122) identifies a project by git remote or root-commit hash, not by path, and every non-git directory collapses to the literal id `global` (packages/core/src/project.ts:112 with packages/core/src/session.ts:448-464); `ProjectDirectoryTable` keys on (project_id, directory) with `directory` realpath'd (packages/core/src/project/directories.ts:65-82), and realpath cannot unify a bind-mount or same-inode alias — the exact `/media/keer/办公/aigcfroge` vs `/media/win_data/aigcfroge` case the review reported; `LocationServiceMap` keys on the raw `Location.Ref` struct (packages/core/src/location-layer.ts:101), so two spellings of one physical directory get two Location-scoped service graphs, and `sameLocation` in packages/core/src/permission/approval-presence.ts:98-100 is raw `===` on the directory string. OWNER RULING 2026-09-19: ADR-25 is Accepted for a migration-free first version: typed unknown baseline, `proved` only from equal realpaths or equal device+inode in the same backend namespace; no `different`, no durable alias relation, no App realpath, no LocationServiceMap-key change.
path-identity.unlock: implement the accepted migration-free slice: annotated Schema contract and round-trip tests; Location-scoped Core resolver using FSUtil realPath/stat; existing instance HttpApi endpoint with OpenAPI identifier; regenerated SDK plus a callable-method assertion; E2 cases for realpath proof, device+inode proof, ENOENT/EACCES/inode-unavailable/not-equal unknowns. Consumption that changes grouping/permission/service-map keys remains separately gated.

project-invalid-path.scope: plan §11.1 requires invalid and inaccessible paths to be handled, and registration accepts any string: `createServerProjects.open` (packages/app/src/context/server.tsx) validates nothing (it now normalizes spelling via pathKey and that is all it claims), the native picker returns whatever the OS dialog gave with no server check (packages/app/src/components/directory-picker.tsx:24-27), and the V2 picker only verifies that it could list the navigated root (packages/app/src/components/dialog-select-directory-v2.tsx:57,107-135,357). A directory the server cannot read is therefore registered and only fails later, at session load, where the failure is per-directory toasts rather than an answer about the path.
project-invalid-path.unlock: needs a way to ask the backend whether a directory is usable before it is trusted — which brushes `path-identity`, so the same §22-2 ADR is the gate — then a typed failure at add time instead of a silent registration. Mock first: `GET /path` always answers with config.directory (packages/app/e2e/utils/mock-server.ts:65-71), so no test can express an inaccessible path today.

project-fanout-on-home.scope: Home load fans out per registered project: ~2N+2 requests at N=500 and N=2000 in the measurement above (/path N+1, /lsp N, /session N+1, provider requests at least 2 each), and the time-to-rows slope (~10-20ms per project, same order as run-to-run variance) tracks that fan-out rather than the list rendering. Nothing errors, so this is a scalability cost and not a defect; it is registered because §16.3 owns performance evidence and because 'the list is unbounded' would otherwise be treated as the cause.
project-fanout-on-home.unlock: S11's performance pass: measure Home with the production benchmark harness rather than the dev server, decide whether the per-project work needs batching, lazy loading or a bound, and report comparable before/after data. Do not set a machine-dependent threshold.
